title: Why a Line's Slope Is Constant

steps.body: For a straight line, the rate of change — its **slope** — is the SAME no matter which two points you pick. Pick a small step or a big step along the line: the rise-to-run ratio always comes out equal. That's what makes it a straight line.

widget.prompt: Why does a straight line have one constant slope?

panels.title: Step 1
panels.body: Draw a small right triangle under the line: run 1, rise 2. The ratio is 2/1 = 2.

panels.title: Step 2
panels.body: Draw a bigger triangle further along: run 3, rise 6. The ratio is 6/3 = 2 — the same!

panels.title: Step 3
panels.body: The two triangles are the same shape (similar), just different sizes — so their rise/run ratios must be equal. That shared ratio IS the slope.

widget.successFeedback: Exactly — similar triangles guarantee the ratio, and so the slope, stays constant.

steps.body: This is why you can compute a line's slope from ANY two points on it and always get the same answer. On the line through (0,0) and (4,8), a small step gives 2, a big step gives 2 — the slope is 2 everywhere.

explanationVariants: Small triangle 3/1 = 3; big triangle 9/3 = 3 — equal, so the slope is 3.
Both triangles on the same line give the same ratio, 3.

widget.prompt: On a line, a small triangle has rise 3, run 1. A bigger triangle on the same line has run 3. What is its rise?

commonErrors.feedback: The bigger triangle must keep the SAME ratio (3): with run 3, the rise is 3×3=9, not 3.
Check the ratio — the small triangle gives 3/1=3, so run 3 needs rise 3×3=9 to match.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The slope is 3/1=3, so a run of 3 must have rise 3×3=9 to keep the same ratio.

steps.body: Slope from two points on a line.

widget.prompt: Build the slope triangle from A so the line also passes through B (1, 1) → (4, 7).

commonPairs.feedback: A run of 3 and a rise of 3 is slope 1 — that reads the run twice. From A to B the rise is 7 − 1 = 6, not 3.
Run 6 and rise 3 is slope 1/2 — the legs are swapped. Slope is the VERTICAL change over the horizontal one: 6 ÷ 3.

widget.fallbackFeedback: From A to B the line travels 3 across and 6 up, so rise ÷ run = 6 ÷ 3 = 2.
widget.successFeedback: Slope 2 — and 1 and 2, 2 and 4, or 3 and 6 all land the line on B. Every triangle on this one line shares its ratio, which is exactly why a line has a single slope.

predict.prompt: The line through (1, 1) and (4, 7) climbs 6 while running across 3. Before you compute — what is its slope?

options.label: 2 — the climb per single step across
6 — the climb is what slope measures
9 — the climb and the run together

predict.reveal: Slope is the climb for ONE step across, not the whole climb: 6 spread over 3 steps is 2 per step. That is why the triangle's two legs are divided, never added.

steps.body: Same line, different points, same slope.
explanationVariants: Any two points on this line give slope 3 — that's the constant-slope property.

widget.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (2, 3) and (5, 12).

commonErrors.feedback: That's just the rise (12−3=9) — divide by the run (5−2=3): 9÷3=3.
Recompute — rise is 12−3=9, run is 5−2=3, so slope is 9÷3=3.

explanationVariants: Through (0,0) and (3,2): rise 2, run 3, slope 2/3 — a valid slope, just shallow.

widget.prompt: What is the slope of the line through (0, 0) and (3, 2)?

options.feedback: Right — rise 2 over run 3 gives the slope 2/3.
That flips rise and run — slope is rise÷run = 2÷3 = 2/3, not 3/2.
That would need rise to equal run, but rise is 2 and run is 3 — the slope is 2/3.
That adds rise and run instead of dividing — slope is 2÷3 = 2/3.

steps.body: Use the constant slope to find a new point on the line.
explanationVariants: Slope from (−2,1) to (2,9): rise 8, run 4, slope 8÷4 = 2. From (2,9), x = 5 is 3 more across, so y = 9 + 2×3 = 15.
The slope stays 2 everywhere on this line, so stepping 3 more across from (2,9) adds 2×3=6 to y: 9+6=15.

widget.prompt: A line passes through (−2, 1) and (2, 9). The point (5, y) is also on this line. What is y?

commonErrors.feedback: 6 is only the rise ADDED from (2,9) out to x=5 — add it to the known y: 9+6=15.
That subtracts the added rise instead of adding it — moving to a LARGER x means y goes UP: 9+6=15, not 9−6.

widget.fallbackFeedback: First find the slope: rise 9−1=8, run 2−(−2)=4, slope 8÷4=2. From (2,9), x=5 is 3 more across, so y = 9+2×3 = 15.

steps.body: A straight line's slope is constant because similar triangles keep the ratio equal.
takeaways: Any two points on a line give the same slope.
Similar triangles on the line share the same rise/run ratio.
That shared ratio IS the line's slope.

concept.body: A straight line has ONE constant slope: similar triangles anywhere along it share the same rise÷run ratio. So any two points give the same slope = rise ÷ run.

widget.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 8).

commonErrors.feedback: That's just the rise (8−2=6) — divide by the run (4−1=3): 6÷3=2.
That's just the run — slope is rise÷run = 6÷3 = 2.
